A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 43-page versions of World-in-World, including Appendices A-F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of their methods, equations, experiments, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original closed-loop experiments on active recognition, image-goal navigation, embodied question answering, and robotic manipulation, together with scaling studies and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including the benchmark results in Tables 1-3, ablations in Tables 4-5, and scaling results in Figures 6-7.

M1.justification: The proposal-simulation-revision planning procedure, unified action API, post-training formulation, and dataset-construction algorithm are unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices B-D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four embodied tasks and the same Matterport3D, HM3D, OpenEQA, and RLBench coverage. No training domain or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated base policies and world-model comparators in Tables 1-3 and 5 are identical. Comparator membership remains unchanged within each reported experiment.

E3.justification: Task splits, episode counts, action budgets, evaluation metrics, planning settings, and post-training configurations remain unchanged, including the detailed protocols in Appendices B-D.

E4.justification: The controllability analysis, data and inference scaling studies, panorama-versus-front-view ablation, InternVL3 policy comparison, and prediction case studies in Appendix E are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed specifications, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests to the existing results.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation scores in Tables 1-5, plotted results in Figures 2 and 5-7, and qualitative predictions in Appendix E are unchanged. No result entries or findings are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Planning equations (1)-(4), metric definitions in Appendix B, the formulation in Appendix C.1, and the sampling definitions and Algorithm 1 in Appendix D are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same benchmark and interface contributions and the same central claims concerning controllability, post-training data scaling, and inference-time computation.

C2.justification: The interpretations in Section 3 and limitations in Section 4 are unchanged, including difficulties with generalization, long-horizon planning, physical dynamics, and dependence on proposal and revision policies.

D1.justification: The abstract changes 'Code will be available' to 'Code is available' while retaining the same repository link. This updates reported resource availability; implementation details, training-resource tables, dataset instructions, and appendix prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: The references, related-work discussion in Appendix A, and positioning against earlier benchmarks and world models are unchanged. The new conference-publication header does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the opening date header with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026,' updates the code-availability sentence, and adds a funding acknowledgment after the conclusion. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Presentation changes are limited to the first-page publication/version labeling and an acknowledgment block occupying previously blank space on page 11. Figures, tables, captions, and the remaining page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Replacing the future code-release promise with an availability statement and adding funding disclosure modestly improve reproducibility information and transparency. The scientific methods, evidence, interpretations, and appendices remain unchanged. This limited improvement concerns documentation; the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's completeness or executability.
